rv.q: Jeff Blim’s music and Nick and Matt Lang’s book add up to a narratively messy, gleefully self-indulgent and stupidly enjoyable show.
We all enjoy a grassroots musical theatre success story, so it feels like an uncomfortable truth to acknowledge that the show itself simply isn’t very good.
Judged purely as a piece of musical theatre, on story, on song, on craft, The Guy Who Didn’t Like Musicals is arguably a two-star show.
As a certain police officer once said, The Guy Who Didn’t Like Musicals is “f**kin’ transcendent!” – and utterly unmissable.
To create a world as rich as the one StarKid have, and then take their unique brand of stories to theatres around the world is a testament to their skill and creativity.

cn.t: StarKid's cult musical horror-comedy divides critics with its chaotic, silly energy. While some praise its phenomenal physicality and visceral impact, others find it amounts to less than the sum of its devoted fanbase suggests.

vr.q: The guy who didn't like musicals is one of my favourite shows of theirs.
I have to admit I am a little bit disappointed with this reprisal and I think that might go a little bit harder because it's on a West End stage.
